newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Prices generally easier at New Zealand wool sales.
newsitem.headline: Prices generally easier at New Zealand wool sales.

text.p: Prices were generally easier at the wool sales in Dunedin and Napier on Thursday, Wools of New Zealand said.

The provisional market indicator was unchanged at NZ$4.71 with the fine segment up 27 cents to $8.78, medium segment was down 11 to $4.88 and the strong segment indicator was down four cents at $4.28.
Compared with the last sale in Christchurch on September 20, merino fleece 18 micron varied from 5 percent to 10 percent dearer, while the remainder was 2.5 percent cheaper.
Halfbred fleece was one percent to two percent cheaper.

Crossbred fleece 33 to 35 microns was one percent cheaper and the remainder was generally two percent cheaper. Second shear was slightly cheaper while bulky skirtings were par to 2.5 percent cheaper. Second shear bellies and pieces were 2.5 percent cheaper. Crutchings were 10 to 15 percent dearer in Napier, but five to 7.5 percent cheaper in Dunedin.

Some 25 percent of the 3,937 clean tonnes on offer failed to meet growers' reserves. Interest came mainly from Western Europe with support from China, Iran, India/Pakistan, Japan, Turkey, Nepal and local mills. The next sale will be on October 3 in Christchurch. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
